title: A Clock in the Factory Museum
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional museum receives a large clock that once hung above the entrance to a local factory.
sentences.ja: 架空の博物館はかつて地元工場の入口に掛かっていた大時計を受け取る。

sentences.en: The donor describes it as a symbol of progress, because the factory had provided employment for many residents.
sentences.ja: 寄贈者は工場が多くの住民に雇用を提供したため進歩の象徴と述べる。

sentences.en: The curator wonders whether the same object might also reveal something about the organization of people's working lives.
sentences.ja: 学芸員は同じ物が人々の労働生活の仕組みについても何か明らかにするか考える。

sentences.en: She decides to investigate the clock's use before writing the label that will accompany the exhibit.
sentences.ja: 展示に添える説明を書く前に時計の使用を調べることにする。

sentences.en: Surviving schedules indicate that workers were expected to arrive before a particular time each morning.
sentences.ja: 残った日程表は労働者が毎朝特定時刻前に到着することを求められたと示す。

sentences.en: A collection of letters includes complaints about penalties for late arrival, alongside accounts of reliable wages and predictable working hours.
sentences.ja: 手紙集には遅刻の罰への苦情と安定した賃金や予測可能な労働時間についての記述がある。

sentences.en: The curator recognizes that the evidence reflects different aspects of the same institution rather than a straightforward opposition between progress and exploitation.
sentences.ja: 証拠は進歩と搾取の単純な対立でなく同じ組織の異なる側面を反映すると認識する。

sentences.en: She also notes that the surviving documents cannot establish how every worker experienced the factory.
sentences.ja: 残存文書で全労働者の工場体験は確定できないとも指摘する。

sentences.en: The exhibition pairs the clock with copies of several original documents and a diagram of the former factory building.
sentences.ja: 展示は時計と複数の原資料の写し、旧工場建物の図を組み合わせる。

sentences.en: Visitors are invited to compare what these sources reveal about the relationship between time, income, and authority.
sentences.ja: 資料が時間、収入、権限の関係について何を示すか比較するよう促す。

sentences.en: Rather than treating the object as a decorative illustration of an already completed historical account, the curator uses it to generate questions.
sentences.ja: 完成した歴史説明の装飾的イラストと扱わず問いを生むために使う。

sentences.en: The label identifies which interpretations are supported by records and which would require additional evidence.
sentences.ja: どの解釈が記録に支えられ、どれが追加根拠を必要とするか示す。

sentences.en: Some visitors expect the museum to celebrate the achievements of local industry, whereas others hope it will emphasize difficult working conditions.
sentences.ja: 地元産業の成果を祝ってほしい来館者もいれば厳しい労働条件を重視してほしい人もいる。

sentences.en: The curator explains that the exhibition need not deny one aspect in order to investigate another.
sentences.ja: 別の側面を調べるため一方を否定する必要はないと説明する。

sentences.en: She welcomes further contributions but distinguishes memories of the factory from independently verified historical details.
sentences.ja: さらなる提供を歓迎するが工場の記憶と独立に確認された歴史的詳細を区別する。

sentences.en: This procedure allows the exhibition to develop without claiming that every contribution carries equal evidential weight.
sentences.ja: 全提供資料が同等の証拠力を持つと主張せず展示を発展させる。

sentences.en: The clock illustrates how an ordinary object can become a starting point for historical inquiry.
sentences.ja: 時計は普通の物が歴史研究の出発点になり得ると示す。

sentences.en: Its significance cannot be fully understood without considering the arrangements in which it once operated.
sentences.ja: かつて使われた仕組みを考えず重要性を完全に理解できない。

sentences.en: A museum can preserve an artifact while encouraging visitors to question the meanings attached to it over time.
sentences.ja: 博物館は工芸品を保存しつつ時を経て付与された意味に疑問を持つよう促せる。

sentences.en: Historical interpretation is enriched when material objects are connected with evidence about the lives of people who used them.
sentences.ja: 物がそれを使った人々の生活の根拠と結びつくと歴史解釈が豊かになる。

vocabulary.definition: things given to a shared effort

questions.prompt: What does the curator want to learn?
options: How the object relates to working lives.

questions.prompt: Why not describe the factory solely as progress or exploitation?
options: The letters prove nothing can be learned.
The factory did not employ people.

questions.prompt: Why use the clock to generate questions?
options: Artifacts can prompt investigation beyond illustration.
The clock has no historical value.
A new factory in the museum.
Celebration of industry or attention to difficult conditions.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish memories from verified details?

options: All objects have one obvious meaning.
Historical research should ignore ordinary artifacts.
Objects gain historical meaning through evidence about their use.

paraphrases.rewrite: The evidence shows different sides of one institution, not merely two opposed judgments.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 単純な二分法を避ける。

paraphrases.rewrite: The clock's meaning depends partly on the system in which it was used.
